messages:
alex: heads up — we hit a surprising case in yesterday's canary where two routing rules matched and the traffic splitter didn't follow the expected weight. think it's the header override + tenant rule tiebreaker.
mina: ugh. can you paste the request headers + route config?
ravi: from logs: ``GET /v1/generate host:api.redwood.test x-tenant:acme x-experiment:canary-42`` routing config: rule A (header x-experiment contains canary-42 -> weight 10%), rule B (tenant acme -> weight 100% for prod)
alex: right — rule B should normally take precedence (tenant-level higher priority) but our splitter evaluated weights and ended up sending to rule A because of fractional sampling + residual bucket rounding.
mina: so it's not a pure precedence bug, it's sampler math + ordering. messy.
sam (eng-platform): can we change sampler to deterministic hashing order-by-priority instead of sequential bucket subtraction? that would avoid leftover rounding favoring lower-priority tiny weights.
ravi: that could work. implementation-wise: compute cumulative weight in priority order, hash -> pick bucket. currently we compute global sum then allocate per-match.
alex: folding in priority means higher-priority rules get exclusive segments first. sounds correct semantically, but will change existing traffic slices slightly. need migration note.
mina: also want to insist on clearer console UX: show the final applied rule in the request inspector and why (e.g., "matched rule B due to tenant precedence; sampling bucket 0.023 => rule A skipped"). customers keep asking "which rule actually served my request".
ops-bot: deploy: routing-sampler-priority-fix started by sam — CI run 14/20 passed :construction:
sam (eng-platform): working on two parts: 1) algorithm change (deterministic priority-slice allocation), 2) telemetry markers: include route_match_id, priority_score, and sampling_hash in trace/span. also add a UI field `resolved_route` in the per-request table.
ravi: for telemetry payload, can we keep previous fields for compatibility and just append `resolved_route_v2`? avoids breaking dashboards.
alex: yes, append rather than rename. also add a boolean `tiebreaker_applied` so we can slice queries for incidents.
mina: about quotas: when a lower-priority canary gets rounded up because of residual, it can eat into tenant quota unexpectedly. we should log quota_consume_source = "canary-sampler" when that happens.
sam (eng-platform): good call. I'll add a quota tag and an alert: high-residual-canary-consumption if canary-induced consumption > 5% of tenant quota in 5m.
ravi: testing note — write unit that simulates many small weighted rules and assert priority-first allocation conserves weight and doesn't overflow tenant-only rules. Also a fuzz test for hash collisions.
alex: timeline? can we ship a backend toggled flag + UI annotation in next week?
sam (eng-platform): backend toggle by Thu, UI annotation Friday, staged rollout next Monday. will post PRs.
mina: once deployed, let's run a soft A/B: 10% of requests use new sampler and we compare per-route resolved counts vs old algorithm to confirm drift < 0.5%.
alex: perfect. thanks — sounds safe. ping me on the PR for review. :thumbsup:
